entrypoints.summary: The GET /flag Flask route reads X-Real-IP from request headers and uses it for its internal-client authorization decision.

affected_components.role: The /flag route consumes X-Real-IP, performs the prefix authorization test, and supplies FLAG to the success template.

causal_paths.kind: header-derived authorization to protected template rendering

code_slices.surrounding_context: FLAG is loaded from ./flag.txt; the accepted branch renders flag.tpl with FLAG, while the rejected branch raises Unauthorized.
code_slices.vulnerable: remote_ip is assigned from request.headers.get("X-Real-IP", "0.0.0.0") and checked with startswith("10.25.25.").

negative_controls: An absent header defaults to 0.0.0.0 and follows the Unauthorized branch.
A header not beginning 10.25.25. follows the Unauthorized branch.
observability.positive_marker: The handler invokes flag.tpl rendering with FLAG after the prefix check.

preconditions: The requester must be able to cause the Flask handler to receive a GET /flag request with an X-Real-IP value beginning 10.25.25.
External header preservation or injection through the deployed proxy is not established by the supplied bundle.

trigger_steps.summary: Send a GET request to /flag carrying an X-Real-IP value with the accepted prefix.

capabilities.concept: assert an internal-looking client IP prefix to the authorization handler
obtain the protected flag rendering path

relation_candidates.dst: assert an internal-looking client IP prefix to the authorization handler
relation_candidates.rationale: The handler reads X-Real-IP directly from request headers and accepts values beginning with the configured internal-looking prefix.

relation_candidates.dst: obtain the protected flag rendering path
relation_candidates.rationale: An accepted prefix avoids the Unauthorized branch and reaches the template rendering supplied with FLAG.
relation_candidates.src: assert an internal-looking client IP prefix to the authorization handler

relation_candidates.rationale: FLAG is read from the flag file and passed as the flag template argument on the authorized route.
relation_candidates.src: obtain the protected flag rendering path

relation_candidates.rationale: The source shows the capability exists because authorization relies on a request-supplied header; replacing that identity source with a trusted one would prevent header assertion from satisfying the predicate. This is a source-derived mitigation inference, not a supplied patch.
relation_candidates.src: assert an internal-looking client IP prefix to the authorization handler

impact.attacker_capability: Cause the application to receive a GET /flag request with an accepted X-Real-IP header value.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of the flag value to a requester whose request reaches the handler with an X-Real-IP value beginning 10.25.25.

causal_trace.summary: A GET /flag request can supply an X-Real-IP header, which the handler reads into remote_ip instead of obtaining an address from a connection property.
The internal-client check accepts any received header value whose string begins with 10.25.25., reducing client-identity authorization to an asserted header prefix.
On a matching prefix, the handler bypasses the Unauthorized branch and renders flag.tpl with the FLAG value.

FLAG is loaded from ./flag.txt at application initialization and supplied to the authorized rendering path, enabling disclosure to a requester that can make the handler receive an accepted header value.

failure.operation: Render the protected flag template after a request-header prefix check

primary_invariant.statement: Access to /flag must be granted only to an internal client identity, not merely to a request that asserts an internal-looking X-Real-IP value.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler treats the request-provided X-Real-IP string as remote_ip and authorizes it using startswith("10.25.25.").

quality.review_notes: The primary application source directly establishes the header-based authorization predicate and protected rendering path. The bundle lacks proxy/nginx-host.conf, a request/response trace, and a test run; it therefore does not establish that an external client can preserve or inject X-Real-IP through the public proxy, nor observed exploit execution. No remediation patch is supplied.

remediation.invariant_restored: The internal-client decision must be based on an identity source that an untrusted requester cannot assert through the request header.
mitigation_classes: Bind internal-client authorization to a trusted, authenticated client-identity source rather than a request-supplied X-Real-IP header

oracle.expected_negative: A /flag request without such a header value raises the Unauthorized internal-clients-only response path.
oracle.expected_positive: A /flag request that the application receives with an X-Real-IP value beginning 10.25.25. follows the render_template path supplied with FLAG.
